title: Sell Mineral Rights in Gulfcrest, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Gulfcrest, AL
metaDescription: Gulfcrest, Mobile County mineral owner tied to south Alabama oil history? We give a clear, patient cash offer on your interest.
heroLead: Gulfcrest is a small unincorporated community in Mobile County, part of the same broad stretch of southwest Alabama where oil development around the Citronelle field shaped local mineral ownership for generations.
intro: Interests connected to Gulfcrest often come to us as small fractional shares inherited from a farm or timber tract, sometimes with a decades-old lease attached, sometimes without one. We treat each case individually rather than assuming every Mobile County tract behaves the same way.

sections.heading: Fractional interests in a large legacy field
paragraphs: Fields the size and age of Citronelle typically end up with a large number of small, divided mineral interests over time, as original owners passed their share down through multiple generations of heirs. If your Gulfcrest interest is a small fraction inherited alongside cousins you barely know, that is the normal outcome of this kind of field's long history, not a sign anything unusual happened to your title.

We are set up to research and buy exactly these kinds of small, complicated fractional interests, working through the chain of title methodically rather than treating a small share as not worth the effort.

sections.heading: What we do when documentation is thin
paragraphs: Some Gulfcrest families have lost track of the original paperwork entirely, holding onto nothing more than a family memory that someone once received oil money from this land. We can often reconstruct ownership using Mobile County deed and probate records along with historical field production data, even when your own file is essentially empty.
This takes more time than a straightforward case with full documentation, but it is far from a dead end.

faqs.question: I have no paperwork at all, just a family story about oil money. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can often reconstruct ownership from public deed and probate records even starting with very little documentation of your own.

faqs.question: Why is my interest such a small fraction?
faqs.answer: Large legacy fields like Citronelle typically get divided many times over generations as original owners pass shares to multiple heirs, so small fractions are common and normal.

faqs.question: Where would Gulfcrest deed records be filed?
faqs.answer: With the Mobile County Probate Office, which holds deed and estate records for this and other unincorporated Mobile County communities.

faqs.question: Does a small fractional interest still get a real cash offer?
faqs.answer: Yes, we evaluate and quote fractional interests of any size, though very small shares may take longer to research thoroughly.
